findings.reason: the retry is the only thing that lets this path reach GitHub from a compute node, so a worker that trusts the sentence and calls `_remote_head` as-is gets a hard refusal of every landing on those nodes, which is the failure the helper's fallback exists to prevent.
findings.text: §5 says "`_remote_head` already reads what the remote branch carries with `git ls-remote`, with the port-443 retry compute nodes need (`_port22_refused`, `_port443_env`)", but `_remote_head` (`reckon/crew/merge.py:614-621`) issues a single `ls-remote` and raises `MergeError` on any failure; the port-22 detection and 443 retry sit only inside `_push_and_confirm` (`reckon/crew/merge.py:670-686`), which §5 is not reusing for the read

findings.reason: either the plan adds `reckon/crew/runs.py` (a shared locking module used by every pointer mutation) to the write paths, or it names that the non-blocking acquisition is a new helper in `resumption.py` opening the same `promotion-<run>` lock path; without one of those the worker's only in-scope option is to duplicate the lock path string, and the section's central mechanism is otherwise unimplementable.
findings.text: §6 says "a resume takes the run's promotion lock first, without blocking (`LOCK_NB`) ... If the promotion lock is held, the resume refuses rather than waits", but `_promotion_lock` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:161`) is `_pointer_lock(f"promotion-{run_id}")`, and `_pointer_lock` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:453-462`) takes a plain blocking `flock(LOCK_EX)` with no non-blocking mode; `reckon/crew/runs.py` is not among §6's write paths, so as written the resume blocks until the promotion finishes instead of refusing, and the done-when arm "a resume ... while its promotion lock is held refuses" cannot pass

findings.reason: the done-when's control ("keying the guard on the gate alone refuses it") forces the worker to find a role test, so a wrong choice fails §5's own gate rather than reaching main, though naming `_is_review_run` would remove the search.
findings.text: §5 scopes the refusal to "an implementation run" but names no field or predicate that identifies one, while the composed-review arm requires exactly that distinction; the code already re-exports `_is_review_run` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:198`, defined in `recovery_review_delivery`), and the pointer anchor the section gives (`recovery_review_dispatch.py` near line 641) points at the review-dispatch record's `head`, not at the role

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §5 attributes the port-443 retry to `_remote_head` in `reckon/crew/merge.py`, but that helper has none; the retry lives in `_push_and_confirm`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every arm in both units names a case, the outcome required of it, and its own negative control, including a base-revision arm for the first case of each unit and a control for the composed-review arm.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both units require gate logs under the run directory with a revision-and-command header and a trailing `EXIT=`, which survives the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test names describe the behaviour they check (`test_a_plain_complete_refuses_an_unmerged_head.py`, `test_a_landing_record_waits_for_the_merge.py`), and no section carries plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers into a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's resume refusal is specified as a non-blocking lock, but the promotion lock it names is blocking and the module that would have to gain a non-blocking form is outside the section's write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 delivers one refusal (with the fetch-and-ancestry function it needs) and §6 one landing-record precondition; neither carries an unrelated second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s6's depends-on s5 and s7's depends-on s5 both resolve to the unit that adds the fetch-and-ancestry function, and §5's write paths (`reckon/crew/merge.py`, `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `reckon/crew/refusals.py`, the new test) contain everything §7 says it calls.
